visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions across week three. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: EBIT 200, tax rate 25%, depreciation 40, capex 60, and working capital falls by 20. Unlevered free cash flow?
questions.explain: 150 after tax, + 40 − 60 + 20 = 150. A fall in working capital releases cash; subtracting the 20 instead gives 110.

questions.q: Equity is 80% of the company and costs 10%; debt is 20% and costs 5% before tax; tax is 20%. WACC?
questions.explain: 80% × 10% + 20% × 4% = 8.8%. Using the 5% pre-tax cost of debt gives 9%, the trap Sofia fell into.

questions.q: Final-year free cash flow is 100, long-term growth 2%, discount rate 8%. Terminal value?
questions.explain: Use next year's cash flow: 102 ÷ (8% − 2%) = 1,700. Using 100 instead of 102 gives about 1,667.
questions.explain_at: Both traps avoided: next year's cash flow

questions.q: A levered DCF gives 900m, net debt is 300m, and there are 80m basic and 90m diluted shares. Value per share?
questions.explain: 900 ÷ 90 diluted shares = 10. The debt is already inside levered cash flows, so taking off net debt again gives 6.67.
questions.explain_at: Fourth trap. A levered D-C-F already gives you equity value

questions.q: If a buyer paid €600m for IKB, which earned €61m last year, roughly what P/E is that?
questions.explain: 600 ÷ 61 ≈ 9.8, so about 10x. The price isn't public, so this only holds if the price were €600m.
questions.explain_at: Nicely done, as long as you keep the if
